impact.affected_asset: Host-process memory outside the Wasmtime store.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause memory retention by driving an embedding application's affected C/C++ API paths that use anyref or externref; remote reachability and practical exhaustion conditions are not established by this bundle.
impact.security_effect: Persistent host-memory leak that can degrade availability.

causal_trace.summary: An embedding application uses C/C++ bindings for anyref or externref values in affected Wasmtime releases.

The migration from store-bound ManuallyRooted values to host-allocated OwnedRooted values was not fully reflected in C/C++ ownership semantics; the C++ API also lacked destructors for relevant reference/value types.
The C API unroot operation contained a typo and did not unroot, while host-defined-function return values and idiomatic C++ values could remain unrooted or undisposed.
Leaked OwnedRooted allocations reside outside the store, so destroying the store does not release them and the host retains memory permanently.

failure.operation: Failure to release host-allocated OwnedRooted reference values after C/C++ API use

primary_invariant.statement: Every owned anyref or externref allocation exposed through the C/C++ API must be unrooted or automatically destroyed on all ownership-transfer and return paths.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Affected bindings left OwnedRooted host allocations without an effective release path in explicit unrooting, host-function return handling, or idiomatic C++ object destruction.

quality.review_notes: Mechanism and remediation are supported by the upstream advisory and inspected upstream patch. The patch notes Valgrind-based leak checking and test changes, but this bundle does not provide a standalone testcase plus an observed vulnerable/fixed execution result; no reproducibility oracle is asserted. Network reachability, attacker-controlled invocation frequency, and actual resource-exhaustion threshold remain unspecified.

remediation.invariant_restored: The fix makes wasmtime_val_unroot drop its value, releases embedder-function return values on the Rust side, and adds C++ destructors for ExternRef, AnyRef, and Val so owned host allocations have release paths.
mitigation_classes: C++ RAII destructors for reference and value wrappers

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Use an affected Wasmtime 37.0.0 or 37.0.1 embedding that exercises anyref or externref C/C++ bindings.
data_structure_invariants: OwnedRooted allocations must not outlive all owning C/C++ API values and ownership-transfer paths.
Store destruction is not a valid cleanup backstop for leaked OwnedRooted host allocations.
state_context.state_machine: A C/C++ API reference value transitions from owned/rooted to released by explicit unrooting or C++ destruction; affected paths omit or neutralize that release transition.

target.component: C/C++ API bindings for anyref and externref ownership
